question: Which of the following dance forms is derived from martial arts practices?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Chhau.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance that incorporates martial arts steps and techniques along with dance.**
 
• The dance form is known to originate in the states of Odisha, West Bengal, and Jharkhand.
 
• Chhau dance is a traditional dance form performed by men from Eastern India that enacts episodes from epics including Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• The main objective of this dance form is to celebrate martial arts.
 
• Chhau dance can be classified into three divisions based on the place it is performed; Mayurbhanj Chau of Odisha, Seraikella Chau of Jharkhand, and Purulia Chau of Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jhora:**

 
 
• Jhora dance belongs to the state of Uttarakhand.
 
• It originated in the Kumaon region.
 
• This magical folk dance form binds people of all castes. Everyone enjoys the dance with a peaceful mind.
 
• Jhora dance is usually seen in the evening at weddings or fairs.
 
• As the dancers perform, everyone watching fills up with energy.
 
• Everyone jumps up to join the dance. It is generally performed in the spring season.
 
• People from all around the country come to witness this magnificent folk dance form.
 
• Jhora dance is incomplete without the famous traditional drum known as "Hurka".
 
• Imagine the drum beating in the background and a large group of people dancing their feet on the beats.
 
• The beats are different from traditional Indian drums.
 
 
 
• **Bharatnatyam** :
 
 
• It is the traditional dance of the state of Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• **Ghoomar:**
 
 
• It is a traditional folk dance of Rajasthan, India, and Sindh, Pakistan.
 
• The dance is chiefly performed by veiled women who wear flowing dresses called Ghaghara.
 
• The dance typically involves performers pirouetting while moving in and out of a wide circle.
 
• The word ghoomna describes the twirling movement of the dancers and is the basis of the word Ghoomar.
 
• Ghoomar is often performed on special occasions, such as at weddings and during Holi, and sometimes lasts for hours.
